Bill.BriefDescription: Establishing advisory limits on noneconomic damages awarded against health care providers.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to noneconomic damage awards in actions againsthealth care providers under chapter 7.70 RCW; adding a new section tochapter 7.70 RCW; and creating a new section.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The legislature finds that there is a crisisin the availability and affordability of professional health careliability insurance coverage. The legislature finds that thismalpractice insurance crisis threatens the current and futureavailability and affordability of health care services for the peopleof the state of Washington by preventing and discouraging health careproviders from initiating or continuing their practice in this state.The legislature further finds that an informed jury may consider thata reasonable limitation on the amount of noneconomic damages that maybe awarded in actions against health care providers is necessary toensure the continued availability and affordability of health care bycontaining the increasing costs of malpractice insurance for healthcare providers. Recognizing the authority of the trier of fact in a civil case todetermine the issue of damages, the legislature intends by this act to p. 1 HB 2835establish an advisory limit on the amount of noneconomic damages thatshould be awarded in actions against health care providers. Thelegislature intends that the trier of fact be informed of thelimitation on noneconomic damages established in this act and the factthat the limitation on noneconomic damages is advisory and not bindingon the trier of fact.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 7.70 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The limitation on noneconomic damages contained in subsection(2) of this section is advisory and not binding on the trier of fact. (2)(a) In an action for damages for injury or death occurring as aresult of the provision of health care, the amount of noneconomicdamages awarded to the claimant should not exceed four hundred thousanddollars. July 1st of each year, beginning July 1, 2005, theadministrator for the courts shall adjust the amount specified in thissubsection for inflation in accordance with the method established inRCW 2.12.037. The administrator for the courts shall publish theadjusted figure in the Washington state register. (b) The limitation on noneconomic damages in (a) of this subsectionshould not apply in an action in which the acts or omissions of adefendant were reckless, willful, or wanton. (c) In an action involving more than one defendant where at leastone of the defendant's acts or omissions was reckless, willful, orwanton and the noneconomic damage award exceeds four hundred thousanddollars as provided under (b) of this subsection, the responsibilityfor damages of a defendant whose acts or omissions were not reckless,willful, or wanton should be determined as though that defendant wasresponsible for his or her proportionate share of a noneconomic damageaward of four hundred thousand dollars. (3) The supreme court shall adopt rules governing the process inwhich the jury is informed of the advisory limitation on noneconomicdamages under this section.
